title: Voice and Narrative Distance
text:
Narrative technique in classic fiction often depends on the relationship between the narrator and the reader. An omniscient narrator, who knows the thoughts of every character, can guide the reader's sympathies with remarkable precision. Some novelists, however, prefer a limited perspective, allowing the reader to discover events at the same pace as a single character. This choice shapes not only what is revealed but also how much trust the reader places in the telling.

Authors also use digression deliberately, pausing the plot to comment on society or on the narrator's own opinions. Such digressions may seem leisurely, yet they often carry an ironic edge that undermines the reader's easy assumptions. Consequently, a seemingly simple story can become a subtle study of judgement. Readers who notice these choices gain a richer understanding of the work.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does an omniscient narrator know?
options: Only the future events of the plot

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do authors use deliberately?
options: Avoidance of any mention of the narrator
Very short chapters in every novel

questions.text: Why might a limited perspective affect how much trust the reader places in the telling?
options: The reader only learns what one character perceives, so the account may be incomplete
The reader is given every fact directly by the narrator
The narrator never speaks to the reader at all
The plot is always predictable from the first page

questions.text: What does the author suggest about digressions that seem leisurely?
options: They have no effect on the meaning of the story
They can quietly challenge the reader's assumptions
They are a mistake that editors should always remove
They appear only in modern fiction

vocabulary.definition: the person or voice that tells a story
having complete knowledge of all characters and events
a temporary move away from the main subject of a text
showing a meaning that is the opposite of what is stated

paragraph_translations: Klasik kurgudaki anlatım tekniği çoğu zaman anlatıcı ile okur arasındaki ilişkiye bağlıdır. Her karakterin düşüncelerini bilen her şeyi bilen bir anlatıcı, okurun sempatisini dikkat çekici bir hassasiyetle yönlendirebilir. Bununla birlikte bazı romancılar, okurun olayları tek bir karakterle aynı hızda keşfetmesine izin veren sınırlı bir bakış açısını tercih eder. Bu tercih yalnızca neyin açığa çıkarıldığını değil, okurun anlatıya ne kadar güvendiğini de belirler.

Yazarlar ayrıca bilinçli olarak konudan sapmayı kullanır; olay örgüsünü durdurup toplum veya anlatıcının kendi görüşleri hakkında yorum yaparlar. Bu tür sapmalar rahat görünebilir, ama çoğu zaman okurun kolay varsayımlarını zayıflatan ironik bir tını taşırlar. Sonuç olarak basit görünen bir hikâye, yargı üzerine ince bir incelemeye dönüşebilir. Bu seçimleri fark eden okurlar esere dair daha zengin bir kavrayış kazanır.
